inputs.name: pressure
inputs.tooltip: The pressure reported by the tablet, between 0.0 and 1.0. If you use the mouse, it will be 0.5 when a button is pressed and 0.0 otherwise.

inputs.name: speed1
inputs.tooltip: How fast you currently move. This can change very quickly. Try "print input values" from the "help" menu to get a feeling for the range; negative values are rare but possible for very low speed.

inputs.name: speed2
inputs.tooltip: Same as fine speed, but changes slower. Also look at the "gross speed filter" setting.

inputs.name: random
inputs.tooltip: Fast random noise, changing at each evaluation. Evenly distributed between 0 and 1.

inputs.name: stroke
inputs.tooltip: This input slowly goes from zero to one while you draw a stroke. It can also be configured to jump back to zero periodically while you move. Look at the "stroke duration" and "stroke hold time" settings.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.tooltip: The angle of the stroke, in degrees. The value will stay between 0.0 and 360.0, effectively ignoring turns of 180 degrees.

inputs.name: tilt_declination
inputs.tooltip: Declination of stylus tilt. 0 when stylus is parallel to tablet and 90.0 when it's perpendicular to tablet.

inputs.name: tilt_ascension
inputs.tooltip: Right ascension of stylus tilt. 0 when stylus working end points to you, +90 when rotated 90 degrees clockwise, -90 when rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise.

inputs.name: custom
inputs.tooltip: This is a user defined input. Look at the "custom input" setting for details.

settings.name: opaque
settings.tooltip:
0 means brush is transparent, 1 fully visible
(also known as alpha or opacity)

settings.name: opaque_multiply
settings.tooltip:
This gets multiplied with opaque. You should only change the pressure input of this setting. Use "opaque" instead to make opacity depend on speed.
This setting is responsible to stop painting when there is zero pressure. This is just a convention, the behaviour is identical to "opaque".

settings.name: opaque_linearize
settings.tooltip:
Correct the nonlinearity introduced by blending multiple dabs on top of each other. This correction should get you a linear ("natural") pressure response when pressure is mapped to opaque_multiply, as it is usually done. 0.9 is good for standard strokes, set it smaller if your brush scatters a lot, or higher if you use dabs_per_second.
0.0 the opaque value above is for the individual dabs
1.0 the opaque value above is for the final brush stroke, assuming each pixel gets (dabs_per_radius*2) brushdabs on average during a stroke

settings.name: radius_logarithmic
settings.tooltip:
Basic brush radius (logarithmic)
 0.7 means 2 pixels
 3.0 means 20 pixels

settings.name: hardness
settings.tooltip: Hard brush-circle borders (setting to zero will draw nothing). To reach the maximum hardness, you need to disable Anti-aliasing.

settings.name: anti_aliasing
settings.tooltip:
This setting decreases the hardness when necessary to prevent a pixel staircase effect.
 0.0 disable (for very strong erasers and pixel brushes)
 1.0 blur one pixel (good value)
 5.0 notable blur, thin strokes will disappear

settings.name: dabs_per_basic_radius
settings.tooltip: How many dabs to draw while the pointer moves a distance of one brush radius (more precise: the base value of the radius)

settings.name: dabs_per_actual_radius
settings.tooltip: Same as above, but the radius actually drawn is used, which can change dynamically

settings.name: dabs_per_second
settings.tooltip: Dabs to draw each second, no matter how far the pointer moves

settings.name: radius_by_random
settings.tooltip:
Alter the radius randomly each dab. You can also do this with the by_random input on the radius setting. If you do it here, there are two differences:
1) the opaque value will be corrected such that a big-radius dabs is more transparent
2) it will not change the actual radius seen by dabs_per_actual_radius

settings.name: speed1_slowness
settings.tooltip:
How slow the input fine speed is following the real speed
0.0 change immediately as your speed changes (not recommended, but try it)

settings.name: speed2_slowness
settings.tooltip: Same as "fine speed filter", but note that the range is different

settings.name: speed1_gamma
settings.tooltip:
This changes the reaction of the "fine speed" input to extreme physical speed. You will see the difference best if "fine speed" is mapped to the radius.
-8.0 very fast speed does not increase "fine speed" much more
+8.0 very fast speed increases "fine speed" a lot
For very slow speed the opposite happens.

settings.name: speed2_gamma
settings.tooltip: Same as "fine speed gamma" for gross speed

settings.name: offset_by_random
settings.tooltip:
Add a random offset to the position where each dab is drawn
 0.0 disabled
 1.0 standard deviation is one basic radius away
<0.0 negative values produce no jitter

settings.name: offset_by_speed
settings.tooltip:
Change position depending on pointer speed
= 0 disable
> 0 draw where the pointer moves to
< 0 draw where the pointer comes from

settings.name: offset_by_speed_slowness
settings.tooltip: How slow the offset goes back to zero when the cursor stops moving

settings.name: slow_tracking
settings.tooltip: Slowdown pointer tracking speed. 0 disables it, higher values remove more jitter in cursor movements. Useful for drawing smooth, comic-like outlines.

settings.name: slow_tracking_per_dab
settings.tooltip: Similar as above but at brushdab level (ignoring how much time has past, if brushdabs do not depend on time)

settings.name: tracking_noise
settings.tooltip: Add randomness to the mouse pointer; this usually generates many small lines in random directions; maybe try this together with "slow tracking"

settings.name: color_h
settings.tooltip: Color hue

settings.name: color_s
settings.tooltip: Color saturation

settings.name: color_v
settings.tooltip: Color value (brightness, intensity)

settings.name: restore_color
settings.tooltip:
When selecting a brush, the color can be restored to the color that the brush was saved with.
 0.0 do not modify the active color when selecting this brush
 0.5 change active color towards brush color
 1.0 set the active color to the brush color when selected

settings.name: change_color_h
settings.tooltip:
Change color hue.
-0.1 small clockwise color hue shift
 0.0 disable
 0.5 counterclockwise hue shift by 180 degrees

settings.name: change_color_l
settings.tooltip:
Change the color lightness (luminance) using the HSL color model.
-1.0 blacker
 0.0 disable
 1.0 whiter

settings.name: change_color_hsl_s
settings.tooltip:
Change the color saturation using the HSL color model.
-1.0 more grayish
 0.0 disable
 1.0 more saturated

settings.name: change_color_v
settings.tooltip:
Change the color value (brightness, intensity) using the HSV color model. HSV changes are applied before HSL.
-1.0 darker
 0.0 disable
 1.0 brigher

settings.name: change_color_hsv_s
settings.tooltip:
Change the color saturation using the HSV color model. HSV changes are applied before HSL.
-1.0 more grayish
 0.0 disable
 1.0 more saturated

settings.name: smudge
settings.tooltip:
Paint with the smudge color instead of the brush color. The smudge color is slowly changed to the color you are painting on.
 0.0 do not use the smudge color
 0.5 mix the smudge color with the brush color
 1.0 use only the smudge color

settings.name: smudge_length
settings.tooltip:
This controls how fast the smudge color becomes the color you are painting on.
0.0 immediately update the smudge color (requires more CPU cycles because of the frequent color checks)
0.5 change the smudge color steadily towards the canvas color
1.0 never change the smudge color

settings.name: smudge_radius_log
settings.tooltip:
This modifies the radius of the circle where color is picked up for smudging.
 0.0 use the brush radius
-0.7 half the brush radius (fast, but not always intuitive)
+0.7 twice the brush radius
+1.6 five times the brush radius (slow performance)

settings.name: eraser
settings.tooltip:
how much this tool behaves like an eraser
 0.0 normal painting
 1.0 standard eraser
 0.5 pixels go towards 50% transparency

settings.name: stroke_threshold
settings.tooltip: How much pressure is needed to start a stroke. This affects the stroke input only. Mypaint does not need a minimal pressure to start drawing.

settings.name: stroke_duration_logarithmic
settings.tooltip: How far you have to move until the stroke input reaches 1.0. This value is logarithmic (negative values will not inverse the process).

settings.name: stroke_holdtime
settings.tooltip:
This defines how long the stroke input stays at 1.0. After that it will reset to 0.0 and start growing again, even if the stroke is not yet finished.
2.0 means twice as long as it takes to go from 0.0 to 1.0
9.9 and bigger stands for infinite

settings.name: custom_input
settings.tooltip:
Set the custom input to this value. If it is slowed down, move it towards this value (see below). The idea is that you make this input depend on a mixture of pressure/speed/whatever, and then make other settings depend on this "custom input" instead of repeating this combination everywhere you need it.
If you make it change "by random" you can generate a slow (smooth) random input.

settings.name: custom_input_slowness
settings.tooltip:
How slow the custom input actually follows the desired value (the one above). This happens at brushdab level (ignoring how much time has past, if brushdabs do not depend on time).
0.0 no slowdown (changes apply instantly)

settings.name: elliptical_dab_ratio
settings.tooltip: Aspect ratio of the dabs; must be >= 1.0, where 1.0 means a perfectly round dab. TODO: linearize? start at 0.0 maybe, or log?

settings.name: elliptical_dab_angle
settings.tooltip:
Angle by which elliptical dabs are tilted
 0.0 horizontal dabs
 45.0 45 degrees, turned clockwise
 180.0 horizontal again

settings.name: direction_filter
settings.tooltip: A low value will make the direction input adapt more quickly, a high value will make it smoother

settings.name: lock_alpha
settings.tooltip:
Do not modify the alpha channel of the layer (paint only where there is paint already)
 0.0 normal painting
 0.5 half of the paint gets applied normally
 1.0 alpha channel fully locked

settings.name: stroke_opacity
settings.tooltip: Opacity applied for whole stroke. meaningful only when non-incremental mode is enabled.

settings.name: texture_grain
settings.tooltip: Grain level applied for texture mapping.

settings.name: texture_contrast
settings.tooltip: Contrast level applied for texture mapping.

switches.name: brushmark_specified
switches.displayed_name: Remember brushmark name as a preset.

switches.name: texture_specified
switches.displayed_name: Remember texture name as a preset.

state_contract.range_policy: No metadata range is declared. Null does not authorize clamping or invent a range. Engine runtime bounds are not metadata bounds.
state_contract.reset_policy: reset() requests engine reset; constructor_default does not describe post-stroke_to reset values.

compatibility.unknown_values: This is a known-setting metadata catalog, not a brush-file schema. Reader/writer must preserve unknown settings, inputs, switches, texts and legacy data without silently dropping or clamping them.
compatibility.none_sentinel: The literal None in input limits is FLT_MAX, not zero or JSON null.
